evidence.positive: Against the running app at localhost:62050 (image loop-e7eeafd6c), the mayo-mayo tenant's Epic FHIR R4 base URL and OAuth token endpoint were pointed at a local stub Epic server, and a practitioner row was created in "mayo-mayo".practitioners with epic_user_id='1434' (the ticket's PERID), name 'Smith, John', no linked user, last_refreshed_at NULL. Stub returned an empty searchset Bundle (total=0), which is exactly what makes MayoGetPractitionerR4Command throw RecordNotFoundException. Two triggers were exercised. (1) Sync admin path: POST /api/admin/practitioners/11111111-1111-1111-1111-000000001434/refresh returned HTTP 200 with body {"outcome":"NO_MATCH","practitioner":{..."epicUserId":"1434"...}} and the app log showed 'WARN c.g.o.i.m.c.MayoGetPractitionerR4Command : Unable to find practitioner with PERID: 1434' immediately followed by 'INFO c.g.o.s.PractitionerRefreshService : No FHIR practitioner match for epic user id 1434 during refresh (method: epicUserId: 1434, name: Smith, John)'. No exception escaped, no WARN 'Failed to refresh practitioner' and no stack trace. The DB row went from last_refreshed_at NULL to 2026-08-24 20:45:19.081959, i.e. the attempt was still recorded. (2) Async path, the one in the ticket's Sentry stack: a Mayo surgical SIU^S14 (rormc-siu-s14-before.hl7 with SCH-20 set to 1434^SMITH^JOHN^^^^^^PERSONID) was injected via POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send with X-Tenant-Id: mayo-mayo. ACK was AA, and on the practitioner-refresh executor thread ('[ioner-refresh-1]') the log showed the same pair of lines at 20:47:29.619, with last_refreshed_at updated to 2026-08-24 20:47:29.619783 and no exception logged.
evidence.negative: Inverse case A — a PERID Epic can resolve must not take the no-match branch: the stub was switched to return a searchset Bundle with total=1 carrying a Practitioner and a PractitionerRole, and POST /api/admin/practitioners/11111111-1111-1111-1111-000000009999/refresh returned HTTP 200 {"outcome":"REFRESHED",...,"epicProviderId":"PROV9999","role":"Anesthesiologist","email":"refreshed.stubbed@example.org"}. The log showed only 'INFO PractitionerRefreshService : Successfully refreshed practitioner: epicUserId: 9999, name: Jones, Ada' — no 'No FHIR practitioner match' line for 9999 and no WARN. The DB row was rewritten: name 'Refreshed Stubbed MD', fhir_id 'Practitioner/stub-fhir-id-9999', role 'Anesthesiologist', specialities ["Anesthesiology"]. Inverse case B — a genuine Epic failure must still be reported as a failure and not be swallowed by the new catch: the stub was switched to return HTTP 500 and PERID 1434 was refreshed again. The API returned HTTP 502 {"outcome":"FAILED",...} and the log showed 'WARN PractitionerRefreshService : Failed to refresh practitioner with epic user id: 1434' followed by 'ca.uhn.fhir.rest.server.exceptions.InternalErrorException: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error: stub forced failure' with a full stack trace (the branch that also calls Sentry.captureException). The stub was returned to the empty-bundle mode afterwards.
evidence.red_check: Pre-fix class swap. The literal parent of the fix (5e58b9f3f^) cannot be loaded any more — OR-2723 later refactored this class to return RefreshResult/RefreshOutcome, which PractitionerAdminController now depends on — so the equivalent was built: the shipped source with only the 'catch (RecordNotFoundException e)' block (and its now-unused import) removed, @Slf4j replaced by an explicit LoggerFactory line since lombok is not on the runtime classpath. It was compiled inside the container with javac against /app/jib-classpath-file. The four shipped class files (PractitionerRefreshService.class plus $Lookup, $RefreshOutcome, $RefreshResult) were backed up to /tmp/backup and to scratch/backup-classes, the pre-fix build was copied over /app/classes/com/guided/orci/service/, and the container was restarted (docker restart, not recreate, so the log history is preserved). With the stub back in empty-bundle mode, POST /api/admin/practitioners/11111111-1111-1111-1111-000000001434/refresh then returned HTTP 502 {"outcome":"FAILED"} and the log went red with 'WARN c.g.o.s.PractitionerRefreshService : Failed to refresh practitioner with epic user id: 1434' followed by 'com.guided.orci.integration.RecordNotFoundException: Unable to find practitioner with PERID: 1434 at com.guided.orci.integration.mayo.commands.MayoGetPractitionerR4Command.execute(MayoGetPractitionerR4Command.java:40)' — the Sentry-captured stack from the ticket, reproduced. The shipped classes were then restored from /tmp/backup, md5sums were compared and matched all four files exactly (fa583bf49bf9b13b4a693bb493dcb437 for the outer class), the container was restarted, last_refreshed_at for 1434 was reset to NULL, and the positive case was re-run: HTTP 200 NO_MATCH with the INFO 'No FHIR practitioner match for epic user id 1434' line and last_refreshed_at set to 2026-08-24 20:45:19.081959. The RecordNotFoundException stack appears exactly once in the whole container log — only while the swap was active.

caveats: Mayo's real Epic FHIR endpoint (test-tls.mcc.apix.mayo.edu) is not reachable from this instance, so tenants.mayo.fhir-r4-server-base-url and oauth-token-endpoint were overridden to a local stub and a locally generated RSA keypair was supplied via epic.oauth.key.pub/priv; everything from MayoGetPractitionerR4Command inward is the real code path, but the Epic server responses were synthetic.

sentry.enabled is false on localhost, so no actual Sentry event could be observed; the WARN-with-stack log line emitted on the same branch as Sentry.captureException was used as the observable proxy for Sentry noise.

The red check swapped in the current class minus the RecordNotFoundException catch rather than the literal 5e58b9f3f^ file, because that pre-refactor version no longer links against PractitionerAdminController.
Only the Mayo lookup branch (searchPractitioner by epicUserId, practitioner with no linked user) was exercised; the MGB branch (getPractitioner by clientUserId) was not.
The container was restarted twice for the class swap but never recreated, so the app has been running with the stub Epic config since the start of this validation.

automation.assessment: PractitionerRefreshServiceTest already covers this well at the unit level: testRefreshPractitioner_MayoTenant_NotFound_DoesNotThrow_AndMarksRefreshed asserts NO_MATCH plus save+markAsRefreshed when the search command throws RecordNotFoundException, and sibling tests cover the empty-response and generic-failure branches. What is not locked in is (a) that the NO_MATCH branch does not reach Sentry — the ordering of the two catch blocks is the whole fix and nothing fails if someone reorders or widens them, and (b) the boundary that actually produces the exception in production: an empty FHIR searchset Bundle travelling through MayoGetPractitionerR4Command into the refresh service, and the async HL7-triggered path from the ticket's stack trace. No qa-suite coverage is warranted; this has no UI surface worth an e2e test.
proposed_tests: PractitionerRefreshServiceTest: assert Sentry.captureException is never invoked on the RecordNotFoundException branch (mockStatic on Sentry), and is invoked on the generic-exception branch — this is what breaks if the catch blocks are reordered.
MayoGetPractitionerR4Command unit test: an empty R4 searchset Bundle (total=0) from a stubbed FhirClient throws RecordNotFoundException carrying the PERID in its message.
PractitionerAdminControllerTest: a refresh whose lookup throws RecordNotFoundException returns 200 with outcome NO_MATCH, while a transport failure returns 502 with outcome FAILED.

Mayo SIU processor integration test: an SIU^S14 whose SCH-20 PERSONID has no FHIR Practitioner still ACKs AA and leaves the practitioner marked refreshed, with no exception escaping the async refresh.

jira_comment:
Validated against a throwaway local instance built from e7eeafd6c, mayo-mayo tenant, with the Mayo FHIR R4 and OAuth endpoints pointed at a controlled stub so an unresolvable PERID could be produced on demand.

Positive: a practitioner with epic_user_id 1434 and no FHIR match refreshed cleanly. The admin refresh endpoint returned 200 with outcome NO_MATCH, the log carried only the INFO line "No FHIR practitioner match for epic user id 1434 during refresh", no exception escaped, and last_refreshed_at was still written so the id is not re-queried on every request. The same result was reproduced on the async path from the Sentry stack by injecting a Mayo surgical SIU whose SCH-20 PERSONID was 1434.

Negative: a PERID Epic can resolve took the normal path (200 REFRESHED, record updated, no no-match line), and a genuine Epic failure was still surfaced as a failure - a forced HTTP 500 returned 502 FAILED and logged the warning with a full stack trace.

Red check: the fix was removed from the running app. The RecordNotFoundException catch was stripped from PractitionerRefreshService, compiled inside the container, and swapped into /app/classes. The same request then returned 502 FAILED and logged the exact stack from this ticket - RecordNotFoundException: Unable to find practitioner with PERID: 1434 at MayoGetPractitionerR4Command.execute. The shipped classes were restored, checksums compared and matched, and the positive case re-ran green.

Caveats: Mayo's real Epic endpoint is unreachable from this instance, so Epic responses were stubbed; Sentry is disabled on localhost, so the warning-with-stack log line on the same branch was used as the proxy for Sentry noise.

Automation: the unit coverage for the no-match branch already exists. Worth adding are an assertion that Sentry is not captured on that branch (the catch ordering is the fix), a command-level test that an empty FHIR searchset throws RecordNotFoundException, a controller test for 200 NO_MATCH versus 502 FAILED, and a Mayo SIU test that an unresolvable SCH-20 PERSONID still ACKs and marks the practitioner refreshed.
